_comment: Signal Intake source registry, v1. Every url verified live via direct HTTP GET (browser UA, response body inspected for actual RSS/Atom content) on 2026-09-11. tier: 1 = primary/official government or regulator feed, descending toward general news/trade media. clusters: one or more of the 7 function-axis clusters. Never add a url here without verifying it actually returns feed content.

sources.name: USTR Press Releases
sources.notes: US Trade Representative's own announcements — primary source for tariff actions and negotiations.

sources.name: Federal Register - USTR
sources.notes: Official USTR rule-filings; catches formal actions that don't get a press release.

sources.name: UK Department for Business & Trade
sources.notes: UK government's own trade policy feed.

sources.name: EU Commission Press Corner - Trade
sources.notes: EU's own trade policy announcements.

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.notes: Leading pan-Asian business desk — closes the Asia-Pacific gap other verified sources miss; also covers Asia manufacturing/input disruption.

sources.name: Federal Register - Bureau of Industry and Security
sources.notes: Official Entity List and EAR rule changes.

sources.name: Federal Register - OFAC
sources.notes: Official US sanctions designations.

sources.name: Federal Register - Customs and Border Protection
sources.notes: Official UFLPA Withhold Release Orders and forced-labor enforcement actions.

sources.name: UK HM Treasury / OFSI
sources.notes: UK's sanctions-implementation authority.

sources.name: Federal Reserve - Banking/Consumer Regulatory Policy
sources.notes: US central bank's bank-regulatory actions affecting lending and credit capacity.

sources.name: Bank of England
sources.notes: UK central bank — bank capital and credit policy.

sources.name: European Central Bank
sources.notes: EU central bank — credit conditions affecting trade finance.

sources.name: International Chamber of Commerce
sources.notes: Writes the rules trade-finance instruments run on (UCP, guarantees); publishes the annual Trade Finance Gap survey.

sources.name: Reserve Bank of India
sources.notes: Direct regulator of TReDS itself, plus NBFC/factoring/priority-sector-lending rules. Deliberate India anchor: TReDS is India-specific by design.

sources.name: Supply Chain Dive
sources.notes: Dedicated trade press for sourcing/logistics disruption; also covers M&A and funding among supply-chain-risk vendors.

sources.name: FreightWaves
sources.notes: Freight and logistics market intelligence.

sources.name: gCaptain
sources.notes: Maritime and shipping trade press — chokepoints, port disruption.

sources.name: The Loadstar
sources.notes: Global freight and logistics trade press.

sources.name: EU Commission Press Corner - Taxation and Customs Union
sources.notes: CBAM is administered by DG TAXUD (customs) — its official channel.

sources.name: EU Commission Press Corner - Climate Action
sources.notes: CBAM's climate and ETS-linkage side.

sources.name: Federal Register - Labor Department
sources.notes: Official US labour-compliance rule actions.

sources.name: Fashion Revolution
sources.notes: NGO tracking garment-sector labour and ESG transparency — adjacent to the forced-labor/UFLPA overlap.

sources.name: Crunchbase News
sources.notes: Funding-round coverage for supply-chain-risk and trade-fintech startups (Altana/Resilink/Sourcemap-adjacent).

sources.name: TechCrunch - AI
sources.notes: Funding and competition news for AI-enabled supply-chain and trade-fintech players; also general AI industry coverage.

sources.name: EU Digital Strategy
sources.notes: The EU AI Office's own channel (AI Act implementation).

sources.name: NIST News
sources.notes: Owns the US AI Risk Management Framework.

sources.name: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
sources.notes: UK's AI governance department.

sources.name: MIT Technology Review
sources.notes: Independent journalism and analysis on AI governance globally.
